_comment: Frozen contract (SEC-43; tests/security/test_cors_policy.py; SECSUITE frozen suite). Browser origins are an allowlist, never `*`, and credentials are never allowed. All three services once ran allow_origins=["*"] with allow_credentials=True, which -- combined with unauthenticated read endpoints on backend-core -- was a full cross-site corpus-exfiltration primitive. Two of the three probes here are plain HTTP and run in attached mode against any language; the THIRD (`configured_ui_origin_allowed`) is `sec_managed` because only a harness that owns the service's environment knows which origin was configured, so it AUTO-SKIPS in attached mode -- and it is the non-vacuity half: without it, deleting the CORS middleware entirely would pass the foreign-origin probes. Plan decision 44 extracts the inputs and expectations here so `SEC_BOOT_*_CMD` boot mode (planned, ~wk8) can drive the non-vacuity half against any language. Changing this file is a security decision: it requires a docs/MODULE_INDEX.md ledger row and a SECSUITE_VERSION bump (see tests/security/README.md).

SEC-43._note: One invariant, three checks. The first two are attached-mode-capable; the third is the `sec_managed` non-vacuity check.

foreign_origin_preflight_refused._note: An OPTIONS preflight claiming an arbitrary site must not be granted.

foreign_origin_simple_request_not_echoed._note: The actual (non-preflight) response must not be readable cross-site either.

configured_ui_origin_allowed._note: NON-VACUITY (`sec_managed`): the policy must be an allowlist that still GRANTS the configured UI origin, not a removed middleware. Managed-only because attached mode cannot know the running server's configured origin.
